questions.q: Why is a stuck expense approval a fundamentally different kind of ticket than most tickets earlier in this course?
options: It isn't different — the same data/setup diagnostic steps apply equally
It only happens in Payables, not Expenses
It's a workflow/routing problem rather than a data, setup, or accounting-pipeline problem, so the evidence lives in BPM Worklist instead of a holds tab or interface table
It is always caused by a closed accounting period
questions.explain: This ticket concerns the approval workflow engine (AMX/BPM) rather than a balance, hold, or accounting entry, so the relevant evidence is found in BPM Worklist's routing history.

questions.q: What did the BPM Worklist routing history reveal about the stuck report?
options: It was rejected by the manager
It had already been approved but not updated
It had multiple conflicting approvers
The approval process never successfully assigned a next approver, so nothing was pending with anyone
questions.explain: The routing history showed the approval process failed to build a complete approver chain, leaving the report with no pending task assigned to anyone.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the stuck approval?
options: The employee's HR record had no manager assigned following a recent department transfer, so the manager-based approval rule had nothing to route to
The expense amounts exceeded a limit
The expense report had duplicate receipts
The employee's role was revoked
questions.explain: Because the manager field in the employee's HR record was blank, the standard manager-based approval rule could not determine the first approver.

questions.q: Why did the report end up stuck 'In Progress' rather than failing with an obvious error?
options: Oracle intentionally hides all approval errors from users
Because the report could not satisfy any rule in its rule set (no manager to route to), leaving it in an unresolved state rather than an outright failure
Because the employee had not actually submitted the report
Because BPM Worklist was down
questions.explain: Since the report couldn't satisfy the manager-based rule, the approval process couldn't resolve a next step, leaving it unresolved rather than producing a clear failure message.

questions.q: What was required to actually fix this ticket?
options: A change to the Expenses approval rule configuration itself
Manually approving the report as the Financial Application Administrator
Correcting the employee's manager assignment in HR, then withdrawing and resubmitting the report
Deleting and recreating the expense report
questions.explain: Since the root cause was missing HR data (no manager assigned), the fix required correcting that HR record and then having the report re-evaluate the rule by resubmitting it.
